amendment_reason: Pre-execution hostile review found that dropping left/right side binding does not necessarily make the serialized fact multiset information-theoretically non-identifying: value multiplicities can in principle reveal equality. The historical serialized-bag arm is therefore diagnosed as lacking a value-independent comparison/counting inductive bias for unseen held-out-domain values, not as provably losing semantic information.
scientific_change: Interpret S3 as an access/inductive-bias attribution study, not an information-loss proof. All D1 data, labels, splits, historical arms, model grid, F1/F2 adapter definitions, primary thresholds, and protected test remain unchanged.
removed_hostile_requirement: dropping side binding breaks at least one dev decision / creates a dev label collision
replacement_hostile_requirement: On train/dev-derived serialized examples, consistent reminting of semantic values changes the historical bag-of-token feature identities while leaving F1 generic equality/unknown features invariant. This demonstrates a value-independent comparison inductive bias without asserting that the serialization is information-losing.
clarifications: F1 adds an operation/access bias: group by side and coordinate path, then compare canonical token multisets.
F1 does not add evaluator labels or domain-specific semantic values.
F2 remains a diagnostic exact comparator over F1 features, not a learned-model novelty claim.
The pre-protected train+dev equivalence requirement between F2 and the historical exact typed comparator remains mandatory.
A positive S3 result may establish that explicit generic comparison access is sufficient; it may not establish that raw serialization is information-theoretically insufficient.
outcome_policy: No S3 protected test access before V1.1 hostile tests and implementation are committed and train+dev-only equivalence is green.
